FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides 
and Pesticides Residues Analysis Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division 
Council. 


Thiamethoxam, technical is used in the preparation of insecticidal formulations for agricultural use. 


Thiamethoxam is the accepted common name by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) for 
3-(2-chloro-1,3-thiazol-5-yimethyl)-5-methyl-1,3,5-0xadiazinan-4-ylidene(nitro) amine. 
The empirical and structural formulae and the molecular mass of thiamethoxam are given below: 


Empirical Formula Structural Formula Molecular Mass

Ck? Å ch,

In the formulation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of Insecticides Act, 1968 
and the Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the Insecticides 
Act and Rules, wherever applicable. 


C,H, CIN,O,S 291.7 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised) . The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard 
THIAMETHOXAM, TECHNICAL — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements and the 
methods of sampling and test for thiamethoxam, 
technical. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provisions which 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below: 


IS No. Title

(third revision)

(second revision) 

10946 : 1996 Methods of sampling for technical 


grade pesticides (first revision) 


3 REQUIREMENTS 


3.1 Description 


The material shall be in the form of white to off white 
powder, free from extraneous impurities or added 
modifying agents. 


3.2 The material shall also comply with the 
requirements given in Table 1. 


4 PACKING 


The material shall be packed in mild steel drums 
[see IS 1783 (Part 1)] containers with HDPE liner. The 
container shall also meet the general requirements 
given in IS 8190 (Part 1). 


5 MARKING 


5.1 The containers shall be securely closed and the 
following information shall be marked legibly and 


indelibly on each container in addition to any other 
information as is necessary under the Insecticides Act, 
1968 and Rules framed thereunder: 


a) Name of the material; 

b) Name and address of the manufacturer; 

c) Batch number; 

d) Date of manufacture; 

e) Date of expiry; 

f) Net quantity; 

g) Nominal thiamethoxam content, percent 
(m/m); 

h) Cautionary notice worded as in the 
Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules framed 
thereunder; and 

j) Any other information required under the 


Standards of Weights and Measures 
(Packaged Commodities) Rules, 1977. 


5.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 


5.2.1 The use of the standard mark is governed by the 
provisions of Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 
and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The 
details of conditions under which the licence for the 
use of Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers 
or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of 
Indian Standards.

IS 15983 : 2013 


6 SAMPLING 


Representative samples of the material shall be drawn 
as prescribed in IS 10946. 


7 TEST 


7.1 Tests shall be carried out by the methods referred 


to in col 4 and col 5 of Table 1. 


7.2 Quality of Reagents 


Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and reagent 
grade water (see IS 1070) shall be employed in tests. 


NOTE—‘Pure chemicals’ shall mean chemicals that do not 
contain impurities which affect the results of analysis. 


ANNEX A 
[Table 1, SI No. (i)] 


DETERMINATION OF THIAMETHOXAM CONTENT 


A-0 GENERAL 


Either of the two methods, namely, high performance 
liquid chromatographic (HPLC) method (see A-1) and 
ultraviolet (UV) spectrophotometric method (see A-2) 
may be used for estimation of thiamethoxam content. 
However, in case of a dispute HPLC method shall be 
the referee method. 


A-1 HIGH PERFORMANCE 
CHROMATOGRAPHY METHOD 


LIQUID 


A-1.1 Principle 


Thiamethoxam content is determined by high 
performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) equipped 
with UV-VIS detector using internal standard 
technique. 


A-1.2 Apparatus 


A-1.2.1 A high performance liquid chromatography 
system equipped with ultraviolet detector, rheodyne 
injector and a printer-plotter-cum-integrator or PC 
based data system is used for this determination. The 
suggested operative parameters are as follows, but can 
be changed if necessary, provided standardization is 
done: 


Column Stainless steel, C-18 (ODS) 
column, 250 mm x 4 mm 
internal diameter 

Temperature Ambient 

Mobile phase Acetonitrile : Water (40 : 60, v/v) 

Flow rate 1.0 ml/ min 

Injection volume : 20ul 

Detector : Ultraviolet detector (256 nm) 


A typical HPLC chromatogram of thiamethoxam, 
technical with internal standard is given in Fig. 1. 


A-1.2.2 Analytical Balance 
A-1.2.3 Microlitre Syringe, 20 ul. 


A-1.2.4 Standard Glassware 


A-1.3 Reagents 
A-1.3.1 Acetonitrile, HPLC/AR grade. 
A-1.3.2 Water, HPLC/AR grade. 


A-1.3.3 Acetophenone (Internal Standard), of known 
purity. 


A-1.3.4 Thiamethoxam Reference Standard, of known 
purity. 


A-1.4 Procedure 
A-1.4.1 Preparation of Internal Standard Solution 


Weigh (and record to the nearest 0.1 mg) about 0.5 g 
of acetophenone into a 100 ml volumetric flask. 
Dissolve and make up the volume up to the mark with 
acetonitrile. Shake well to homogenize. 


A-1.4.2 Preparation of Standard Solution 


Weigh (and record to the nearest 0.1 mg) about 0.2 g 
of thiamethoxam analytical standard into a 50 ml 
volumetric flask. Dissolve and make up the volume up 
to the mark with acetonitrile. Shake well to 
homogenize. Pipette out 5 ml of the above solution 
into another 100 ml volumetric flask, add 5 ml of 
internal standard solution (see A-1.4.1) and make up 
the volume upto the mark with acetonitrile. 


A-1.4.3 Preparation of Sample Solution 


Weigh (and record to the nearest 0.1 mg) about 0.2 g 
of thiamethoxam, technical into a 50 ml volumetric 
flask. Dissolve and make up the volume upto the mark 
with acetonitrile. Shake well to homogenize. Pipette 
out 5 ml of the above solution into another 100 ml 
volumetric flask, add 5 ml of internal standard solution 
(see A-1.4.1) and then make up the volume upto the 
mark with acetonitrile.

not deviate from each other by more than 2 percent.

ingredient and the internal standard, and calculate the

Take average values of the peak areas as indicated 
under A-1.5.

A-2 ULTRAVIOLET SPECTROPHOTOMETRIC 
METHOD 
A-2.1 Principle 


Thiamethoxam content is determined by ultraviolet 
spectroscopy (UV). 


A-2.2 Apparatus 


A-2.2.1 Ultraviolet Spectrophotometer (double beam), 
coupled to a printer-plotter and having 10 mm quartz 
cells. 


A-2.2.2 Ultrasonic Bath 
A-2.2.3 Standard Glassware 


A-2.3 Reagents 
A-2.3.1 Methanol, AR grade or equivalent. 


A-2.3.2 Anhydrous Sodium Sulphate, AR grade or 
equivalent. 


A-2.3.3 Thiamethoxam Reference Standard, of known 
purity. 


A-2.4 Procedure 
A-2.4.1 Preparation of Standard Solution 


Weigh accurately 0.040 0-0.042 0 g of thiamethoxam 
analytical standard of known purity into a 200 ml 
volumetric flask. Add 75 ml of methanol and sonicate 
for 10 min. Make up the volume upto the mark with 
methanol. Shake well to homogenize. Pipette out 5 ml 
of this solution into a 100 ml standard volumetric flask 
and dilute up to the mark with methanol. Shake well 
to homogenize. 


A-2.4.2 Preparation of Sample Solution 


Weigh out accurately 0.040 0-0.0420g of 
thiamethoxam, technical and transfer it to a 200 ml 


IS 15983 : 2013 


volumetric flask. Add 75 ml of methanol and sonicate 
for 10 min. Make up the volume upto the mark with 
methanol. Shake well to homogenize. Pipette out 5 ml 
of this solution into a 100 ml standard volumetric flask 
and dilute up to the mark with methanol. Shake well 
to homogenize. 


A-2.4.3 Estimation 


Carry out baseline correction with methanol. Measure 
absorbance of standard solution and sample solution 
at about 255 nm using 10 mm quartz cell. Calculate 
thiamethoxam content as given in A-2.5. 


A-2.5 Calculation 


Thiamethoxam content, percent by mass 


_M À 
j M, À 
where 
M, = mass of standard thiamethoxam in standard 


solution, in g; 


M, = mass of the sample taken for test, in g; 


A, = absorbance of thiamethoxam in the standard 
solution; 
A, = absorbance of thiamethoxam in the sample 


solution; and 


P = percentage purity of thiamethoxam 
reference standard. 


ANNEX B 
[Table 1, SI No. Gii)] 


DETERMINATION OF pH CONTENT 


B-0 PRINCIPLE 


The pH is determined using a pH meter having a range 
0-14 with a precision of 0.1 pH. 


B-1 APPARATUS 


B-1.1 pH Meter, direct reading, with glass electrode 
and a calomel reference electrode or any other suitable 
electrode, along with temperature compensation. 


B-1.2 Balance (Analytical), sensitive to 0.1 g. 
B-1.3 Magnetic Stirrer 

B-1.4 Buffer Tablets, tablets of pH 4.0 and 7.0. 
B-1.5 Standard Glassware Beaker 

B-1.6 Wash Bottle, containing distilled water. 


B-2 PROCEDURE 


From the buffer tablets, prepare 4.0 and 7.0 pH buffer 
solutions, following the prescribed instruction given 
with the tablets. 


Calibrate the pH meter using the buffers as follows: 


Immerse the electrodes of the pH meter in 7.0 pH buffer 
solution and adjust the meter to read 7.0 pH. Remove 
the buffer solution from the electrodes, wash these with 
water and wipe the electrodes free from water. 


Replace with pH buffer solution 4.0 and adjust the 
meter to read 4.0 pH. Remove the buffer solution from 
the electrodes, wash these with water and wipe the 
electrodes free from water. 


Weigh accurately about 1.0 g of the sample in a 250 ml 
glass beaker. Add 100 ml of distilled water. Mix the 
sample thoroughly to get a uniform suspension in a 
beaker. Stir the dispersion for 1 min on a magnetic 
stirrer at a minimum speed. Immerse the electrodes 
(in case of a combined glass electrode, the diaphragm 
should be below the level of the liquid). Stir for further 
30 s at the slowest speed. 


Immerse the electrodes (in case of a combined glass 
electrode, the diaphragm should be below the level of 
the liquid). Stir for further 30 s at the slowest speed. 
Measure the pH of the suspension and report result to 
nearest 0.1 pH.
